source: Written for islamic-studies/y10 lesson 26 (Pupil PDF worksheet: exemption case studies)
intro: Lesson 26: 3.3 Those exempt from fasting. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

head: Person
Exempt or not? What they do? Evidence
rows: A diabetic who must eat regularly
A grandfather of 90 who cannot fast

blocks.answers: 1. Exempt if medical advice says so; fidyah if the condition is permanent (2:184). 2. A traveller: may break the fast and make up the days later (2:184). 3. Not required before adulthood; trained gently. 4. Fidyah: feed a poor person for each day (2:184). 5. Not exempt: exams are not a reason in the texts; plan rest and study. 6. Not exempt for work alone; may break only if genuinely harmed, then make up the days.

panels.title: Set passage again: 2:184-185
points: 'Whoever is ill or on a journey: other days'
'Upon those who are able only with hardship: fidyah'

keywords.def: a concession: an easing Allah allows
feeding a poor person for each day missed by those who cannot fast

questions.q: Explain the difference between qada' and fidyah. (4 marks, our own question)
questions.a: Qada' is making up the missed days later, for temporary reasons (illness, travel); fidyah is feeding a poor person for each day, for those who can never fast (elderly, permanent illness), from 2:184.

questions.q: A traveller who breaks the fast must ...

Case studies on the pupil PDF: six people (a diabetic who must eat regularly; a pilot flying long-haul; a ten-year-old; a grandfather of 90; a student with exams; a nurse on night shifts). For each: exempt or not, what they do, and the evidence. Then a 6-mark answer in the portal response box: 'Explain why some Muslims are exempt from fasting.'
questions.a: Diabetic: exempt if medical advice says so, fidyah if permanent; pilot: traveller, may make up; child: not required; grandfather: fidyah; student: not exempt; nurse: not exempt unless harm; 6-mark with 2:184-185 and 2:286

questions.q: Extend: why do scholars differ about pregnant and breastfeeding women?
questions.a: The texts can be read as qada', fidyah, or both, depending on whether the fear is for the mother or the child

questions.q: An elderly man who can never fast ...
questions.a: A) Pays fidyah. Fidyah is for those who cannot fast and cannot make up (2:184).

questions.q: Think again: why does Allah excuse anyone?
questions.a: He is Merciful and Just and does not burden beyond capacity
